newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore traders buy record 1.9 mln bbls diesel.
newsitem.headline: Singapore traders buy record 1.9 mln bbls diesel.

text.p: A record 1.9 million barrels of diesel for end April/early May lifting exchanged hands in the Singapore spot market on Friday, breaking the last single-day record of 1.35 million barrels set on Tuesday, traders said.
They said two related Singapore oil trading firms and a Japanese trader were involved in purchasing the 12 cargoes.
The sellers included a Swiss trader with three cargoes, a French refiner with four cargoes, a European major with two cargoes and a Mediterranean trader with one cargo.
The prices ranged between $26.95 and $27.20 per barrel for end April cargoes, free-on-board (fob) basis, while early May cargoes traded between $26.70 and $26.80.
The local traders have to date bought at least a staggering 13 million barrels since March 3.
This has helped boost regional diesel prices and support refining margins.
But some traders expressed unhappiness that a limited number of buyers were able to dominate the market.
"This is unhealthy," one trader said. "When is this going to end, when the industry stops and has to sell to one party?"
